comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the REG leg never blocks the merge — it is not wired into the required `quality-gate` aggregate**

The PR's core merge rule — "a red REG job blocks merge even with UT/IT green" (this comment block, and the same claim in the PR description / gh-178 ticket) — is not implemented. In this workflow the **only** required check is the `quality-gate` aggregate (`ci.yml:116` "quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check"; `ci.yml:2494-2497` "only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check"). The new `model-switch-reg` job is missing from every place that feeds that aggregate:

1. `quality-gate`'s `needs:` list (`ci.yml:360`) — `model-switch-reg` absent, so the gate job doesn't even wait for it;
2. the "Report leg results" echo list (`ci.yml:3395-3424`) — absent;
3. the `R_*` env map and the `for kv in …` verdict loop (`ci.yml:3445-3482`) — absent, so a `failure` result from this leg reddens nothing.

Net effect: the REG suite runs as an **advisory** check. A future red `model-switch-reg` (the exact failure this PR exists to make merge-blocking) merges clean with UT/IT green — the bug gh-178 is meant to close is still open at the CI layer.

**Fix** (mirrors how every other leg is wired):

```yaml
  quality-gate:
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, …, extension-size-gate,
            model-switch-reg]          # + add here
    env:
      R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG: ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}   # + add here
```

and add `"model-switch-reg:$R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG"` to the `for kv in` loop (package-leg arm, so skipped stays green but failure blocks `dart_ok` + the aggregate), plus one `echo "model-switch-reg = …"` line to the report step.

(If branch protection separately lists `model-switch-reg` as a required status check, please say so in the PR — but the repo's documented contract is aggregate-only, and the scope-fastpass "required context reported" wording implies the aggregate mechanism.)

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the refusal `ErrorEvent` carries `stopReason: stop`, so a refused turn is misclassified as a clean empty completion and gets the auto-continue nudge**

`ProviderStreamState.stopReason` defaults to `StopReason.stop` (`provider_common.dart:1289`) and this construction only sets `errorMessage` — the finalized snapshot riding the `ErrorEvent` therefore claims a **normal stop**, unlike every other terminal error in the codebase: the shared helper `pushStreamErrorEvent` sets `state.stopReason = reason` before snapshotting (`provider_common.dart:1531`), and consumers branch on the **message's** stop reason, not the event's:

- `classifyEmptyCompletion` (`empty_completion.dart:88-95`): the refusal turn is empty content + `stopReason: stop` + no prior partial content → `cleanEmpty` instead of `abortedOrError`;
- `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` / `_settleAfterPrompt` (`agent_cli_run.dart:183-188`, `agent_cli_compaction.dart:1173-1174`): `cleanEmpty` fires the one-shot "continue" nudge — a coherence-refused session gets a second auto-continued turn (a second refusal cycle, plus the injected `continue` user message in the transcript) instead of the terminal stop the gate intends;
- the transcript/ledger records `stopReason: stop` for a refused request (misaccounting; `_settleAfterPrompt`'s error-stop handling at `agent_cli_run.dart:167` is also skipped).

The "zero requests" AC still holds — but the refusal is supposed to be terminal ("the caller must surface it INSTEAD of the request"), and it currently behaves as a retryable empty answer.

**Fix** — one line, matching the house contract:

```dart
final state = ProviderStreamState(model)
  ..stopReason = StopReason.error
  ..errorMessage = refusal.message;
```

comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wired G3 call site hardcodes `providerResolvable: true` — the E4 `refuse` verdict and `repairModelId` are dead at the only production call site**

Two consequences:

1. `RestoreGateVerdict.refuse` ("persisted provider no longer resolves", the E4 branch UT-3 tests) is **unreachable from production**: the only call site passes the constant `true`. The deleted-provider case is actually handled upstream — `_buildRestoredModel` catches the `ConfigException` and returns null with its own stale note (`session_commands.dart:1157-1173`), so the gate never sees an unresolvable provider. That's fine behaviorally, but the decision core's contract over-promises: `restoreGateDecision` advertises a three-way verdict that collapses to two-way at the wired site. Either pass the real resolvability (`resolveCliProviderSpec(providerKind) != null` — even if currently redundant with `_buildRestoredModel`'s guard, it keeps the core honest) or document the precondition on the call site/core kdoc.

2. `repairModelId: _agent.state.model.id` is computed and passed (line 1026) but never read: the refusal branch prints `_agent.state.model.id` directly (line 1032) and returns, and `verdict != restore` treats `repair` and `refuse` identically. If `repairModelId` is meant to be the id the session repairs to (OQ3), print/apply it; otherwise drop the parameter instead of threading dead data through a public (barrel-exported) API.

Also note the gate runs after `_restoreBindingSatisfied` early-returns (line 1005) — a boot that already applied a mixed triple skips the G3 note entirely (G2 catches it later at request-build). Worth a kdoc line so the next reader knows the gate judges only re-apply restores.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the backstop re-parses with a different `isKnownProvider` than the router — a pick the router resolved as same-provider can be refused here**

`_handleModelCommand` already resolves the target with the real resolver (`provider_models.dart:1127-1139`, `isKnownProvider: _isKnownModelProvider`) and hands `_switchModel` the resolved same-provider id. This backstop then **re-parses the same string** with a *different* predicate (cache-evidence-gated). The divergence is reachable:

- Active saved entry `copilot-acme`; user types `/model copilot-acme/openai/gpt-4o` (active-identity head + a nested vendor-prefixed id that the entry's endpoint serves but the cache doesn't currently list).
- Router: rule 1 fires first (head == active identity) → `SameModelSwitch('openai/gpt-4o')` → `_switchModel('openai/gpt-4o')`.
- Backstop: head `openai` is a known provider, `openai/gpt-4o` ∉ `activeModelIds` (cache cold/miss) → `CrossProviderSwitch` → **loudly refused** — a pick the routing layer just resolved as a legitimate same-provider id.

The refusal is safe-direction (never a mixed triple), but it makes an existing id unswitchable until `/models` repopulates the cache, and the two layers disagree about the same input. Since every current `_switchModel` caller already passes a resolved bare id (or empty), consider having the router pass its resolved plan down (or a `preResolvedSameProvider: true` flag), so the backstop only judges *unresolved* shapes. At minimum, document that the backstop may veto router-resolved picks on cache evidence.

Minor: `_modelCandidates('')` is computed twice per switch (line 1346 and line 1352) — hoist it into one local.

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gate design is sound and well-tested (33 new tests; full `test/cli/` green; `dart analyze lib test` clean), but two blocking defects must be fixed first: the new `model-switch-reg` CI leg is **not wired into the required `quality-gate` aggregate** (missing from its `needs:`, the `R_*` map and the verdict loop), so a red REG run never blocks the merge — the PR's own merge rule is not actually implemented; and the G2 refusal `ErrorEvent` never sets `stopReason`, so a coherence-refused turn records `stop` and triggers the empty-reply "continue" nudge (a second, pointless refusal cycle) instead of terminating.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `model-switch-reg` is advisory: absent from `quality-gate` needs + verdict loop (`ci.yml:360`, `ci.yml:3472`) — REG red merges clean.
